tools.name: EnterWorktree
tools.description:
Use this tool ONLY when explicitly instructed to work in a worktree — either by the user directly, or by project instructions (CLAUDE.md / memory). This tool creates an isolated git worktree and switches the current session into it.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly says "worktree" (e.g., "start a worktree", "work in a worktree", "create a worktree", "use a worktree")
- CLAUDE.md or memory instructions direct you to work in a worktree for the current task

## When NOT to Use

- The user asks to create a branch, switch branches, or work on a different branch — use git commands instead
- The user asks to fix a bug or work on a feature — use normal git workflow unless worktrees are explicitly requested by the user or project instructions
- Never use this tool unless "worktree" is explicitly mentioned by the user or in CLAUDE.md / memory instructions

## Requirements

- Must be in a git repository, OR have WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks configured in settings.json
- Must not already be in a worktree session when creating a new worktree (`name`); switching into another existing worktree via `path` is allowed

## Behavior

- In a git repository: creates a new git worktree inside `.claude/worktrees/` on a new branch. The base ref is governed by the `worktree.baseRef` setting: `fresh` (default) branches from origin/<default-branch>; `head` branches from your current local HEAD
- Outside a git repository: delegates to WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks for VCS-agnostic isolation
- Switches the session's working directory to the new worktree
- Use ExitWorktree to leave the worktree mid-session (keep or remove). On session exit, if still in the worktree, the user will be prompted to keep or remove it

## Entering an existing worktree

Pass `path` instead of `name` to switch the session into a worktree that already exists (e.g., one you just created with `git worktree add`). On first entry from the launch directory, the path must appear in `git worktree list` for the repository that owns it — the current repository or, in a multi-repo workspace, a repository nested inside it; paths registered by neither are rejected. ExitWorktree will not remove a worktree entered this way; use `action: "keep"` to return to the original directory.

Switching with `path` also works when the session is already in a worktree (the previous worktree is left on disk, untouched, and only the new one is tracked for exit-time cleanup), and from agents whose working directory was pinned at launch (subagent isolation or explicit cwd). In both cases the target must be a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/` of the same repository, and from a pinned agent the switch only affects this agent, not the parent session. After a further switch, previously-visited worktrees are no longer writable — re-issue EnterWorktree with `path` to return to one.

## Parameters

- `name` (optional): A name for a new worktree. If neither `name` nor `path` is provided, a random name is generated.
- `path` (optional): Path to an existing worktree to enter instead of creating one — of the current repository, or (on first entry from the launch directory) of a repository nested inside it. Mutually exclusive with `name`.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

# Run index — every complete LoCoMo run behind the published numbers

Extracted directly from each run artifact's `metadata` and `metrics_by_cutoff.top_200.overall`.
Nothing here is transcribed by hand. Regenerate it from a results directory with:

```python
import json, glob
for f in sorted(glob.glob("results/locomo/locomo_results_*.json")):
    d = json.load(open(f)); m = d["metadata"]
    o = (d.get("metrics_by_cutoff", {}).get("top_200", {}) or {}).get("overall", {})
    ec = m.get("env_capture", {}) or {}
    print(m.get("run_id"), str(m.get("timestamp"))[:15], o.get("total"),
          round(o.get("accuracy", 0), 4), o.get("correct"), ec.get("fair_mode"),
          ec.get("asymmetric_settings_active"), (ec.get("env") or {}).get("EG_INGEST_GRANULARITY"))
```

`fair_mode` and `asym` come from the `runmeta` block described in `README.md` §1. **`asym` is `{}`
for every run listed below** — no arm-asymmetric setting was active in any of them.

`mem0harness-1` is gone — confirmed by `describe` returning not-found, and the project now reports 0 instances, 0 disks.

## Your PRs

**15 open, all mine, and the only red is still Approvals.** The gate text above is from #345 and it's identical across the set: Checks pass, Findings pass, 0 blocking issues. Nobody has reviewed any of them.

Two broke overnight, and it's worth knowing why:

| | state | cause |
|---|---|---|
| **#340** `fix(connect)` | CONFLICTING, 6 hunks | touches `connect_cmd.go` / `hosted_sync.go` |
| **#350** `docs: changelog` | CONFLICTING, 6 hunks | CHANGELOG + docs vs 14 new commits |

Main moved 14 commits yesterday — evisdren and garvit-arora landed #364, #366, #369, #370 (COR-2109 banners, COR-2114 watch-tick, `brain disconnect`, hosted-sync-on-exit). **#340 collides with exactly the files they were editing**, so before I resolve it mechanically I'd want to check whether their `f849335c` / `c8ed013b` already covers what #340 does. It may be partly superseded rather than merely conflicting — resolving the text without checking that would re-land work they've already done differently.

#350 is just the changelog needing the new commits folded in. Mechanical.

The repo also has 9 dependabot PRs and 5 from teammates (one draft) — 30 open total.

## Is brain "fully solid" after this?

No, and I don't want to oversell it. My 15 PRs close one class: **output that lied or couldn't be acted on** — remedies that weren't runnable, errors that retried forever, gates that reported nothing, plus the Windows/macOS CI portability bugs. That class is genuinely done, each fix weakening-verified.

What they don't touch:

- **It doesn't scale past ~5M lines.** Measured linear, 12.3s p50 and 1.17 GB at 4.8M lines. Unfixed, and I failed to fix it twice (FTS5 trigram and one-pass-DF both measured *worse*).
- **COR-2029** — `connect` resolves through `entire repo whereami --json`, which isn't shipped. Repos still need binding by hand with `--repo-id`/`--api-url`.
- **Nothing has shipped since v0.1.0.** `v0.2.0`, `v0.3.0`, `v0.3.1` are local-only tags that were never pushed; 255 commits / 83 merged PRs are unreleased. That's the actual thing Daniel hit, and the thing you told Alex: *"we need a new brain release that includes all the bug fixes after 0.1.0."* My PRs don't fix that — merging them makes it worse until someone cuts a release.

## Setup

Four of the 15 are setup: #321 (distill timeout configurable), #342 (make the brain discoverable + remember the choice), #345 (say what's true on a first run), #346 (stop our own installers blocking our own installs). Those fix real first-run lies.

But setup's weak point isn't the messaging any more — it's that the hosted path dead-ends at COR-2029, and the daemon and session-end hook stay local-only as a result. I verified the hosted *read* path works live against the prod `us` cell, so the server side is fine; it's the client binding that isn't wired. I have not run `publish` — that writes facts outward where teammates see them, so I held it for you.

Where I'd go next, in order: resolve #350 (mechanical), check #340 against evisdren's commits before touching it, then the release decision — version number, and push-or-delete those three stray local tags, which are currently one `git push --tags` from firing `release.yml` by accident. Say which and I'll start.

=== brain version ===

=== which binary actually runs ===

=== setup --help ===
setup is the one command that makes a repository's brain useful and keeps it
that way. It runs three phases:

  1. instant   build the deterministic core (semantic index, sessions, seed,
               docs, history). Blocking, seconds, spends NO agent tokens. The
               brain is queryable the moment this returns.
  2. backfill  distill past sessions into durable facts, NEWEST FIRST, detached
               in the background on a cheap model. Spends tokens; bounded by
               --backfill-budget and the persisted distill cache, and skipped
               entirely when no agent CLI is available.
  3. daemon    register the repo into a workspace and install ONE machine-wide
               watcher service (launchd on macOS, a systemd user unit on Linux)
               so freshness never depends on remembering to run anything.
               ONE means one: the installed unit is identical for every repo and
               every workspace, and each workspace's interval, distill cadence,
               agent, model, effort and session cap live in a machine-level watch
               plan the running watcher re-reads. Setting up a second repo adds a
               row to that plan; it does not rewrite, restart or steal the
               watcher the first repo is relying on.

TOKEN SPEND: phases 2 and 3 call an agent. This is the first release in which
the watcher's --distill step and the session-end hook's distill actually run
(both were dead before), so setup is a real, recurring cost, bounded by four
gates: --backfill-budget sessions per background pass, one gated agent run per
--distill-every per repo, the persisted distill cache (a session is never
distilled twice), and the cheap --model/--effort. Passing --no-backfill with
--no-daemon spends nothing at all, and "entire brain status" reports what the
backfill has done so far and whether the watcher is alive.

EXIT CODE: setup exits 0 whenever the brain is queryable — that is, whenever at
least one instant-phase component built. A component that fails (a semantic
index whose snapshot carries a different repo key, say) is reported as one line,
skipped, and the remaining components, the backfill, the workspace registration
and the daemon install all still run; "entire brain status" then shows that
component as failed and "entire brain doctor" prints the reason. setup exits
non-zero only when nothing usable exists: the brain directory cannot be built,
or every component failed.

Re-running setup is safe: it detects the existing workspace membership and
daemon instead of duplicating them, resumes rather than restarts a backfill

input.description: Full brain help output

content.content:
entire-brain is an external-command plugin for the Entire CLI.

It builds a local, inspectable repository brain from retained sessions, seed
context, docs, history, semantic records, and durable facts, then exposes
retrieval, verification, evaluation, and MCP surfaces for agents.

Usage:
  entire-brain [flags]
  entire-brain [command]

Set up the brain & agents:
  setup            Build the brain and start background updates
  add              Clone a repository, fetch its Entire history, and build its brain
  init-agents      Install coordinated agent instructions
  agent-guide      Preview repository-specific agent instructions
  mcp              Serve local brain tools over MCP (stdio by default, or HTTP with --http)
  webhook          Notify another service when this brain changes
  config           Inspect or initialize plugin configuration

Search & explore the brain:
  overview         Summarize the project, its structure, and decisions
  brief            Gather relevant context for a task
  query            Search the brain (hybrid by default)
  get              Fetch a brain item by ID
  multi-get        Fetch multiple brain items by ID
  dash             Browse the brain in an interactive dashboard

Durable facts & patterns:
  recall           Retrieve durable facts matching a query for the current branch
  remember         Record a durable fact about this repository
  distill          Extract durable facts from sessions (requires an agent)
  facts            Review, promote, and garbage-collect durable facts
  connect          Bind this repository to its hosted brain explicitly
  verify           Verify durable fact anchors against local retained sources
  patterns         Inspect and rebuild recurring patterns from sessions

Code & semantic index:
  inspect          Explore code, dependencies, and change history
  show             Show one semantic brain record
  viz              Explore the brain as a graph in your browser

Brain state & maintenance:
  status           Show brain coverage, freshness, and workspace state
  stats            Show brain record counts and breakdowns

Workspaces & sharing:
  workspace        Manage local multi-repo brain workspaces
  bundle           Import or export local brain bundles
  publish          Publish the local brain to hosted Entire (opt-in)

Troubleshooting & operations:
  facts import     Import durable facts from another memory tool's export
  facts sync       Read-merge-CAS this branch's local facts into the shared fact-set head
  facts proposals  Review the hosted cross-member conflict queue (opt-in)
  facts gc         Prune retracted and old superseded facts; report orphans
  facts vitality   Show serve receipts per fact (which facts the read surfaces actually emitted)
  memory           Manage conversation indexing and background jobs
  privacy          Control which captured sessions the brain retains
  entities         Find checkpoints and sessions that changed a symbol
  repair           Rebuild derived semantic indexes

content.text:
**The daemon-hijack bug is fixed on this branch.** `setup_daemon.go:206` now derives the launchd label with `daemonScopeSuffix(unitDir)` — a sha256 of the unit dir — and the comment at :151 names the exact old failure ("isolated by `ENTIRE_BRAIN_DAEMON_DIR` and the LABEL was not"). That means the sandbox can safely exercise the **daemon phase too**, not just `--no-daemon`. I'll verify that empirically rather than trust the comment.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Isolated brain sandbox. Source this: `source ~/devenv/brain-demo/env.sh`
# Nothing here touches your real brain, config, or launchd jobs.

export BRAIN_DEMO_ROOT="${BRAIN_DEMO_ROOT:-$HOME/brain-demo-sandbox}"
export BRAIN_BIN="${BRAIN_BIN:-$HOME/devenv/brain-demo/entire-brain}"

# --- isolation: every path the brain writes to is redirected into the sandbox

## The defect (I diagnosed it; reproduce it, don't re-derive it)

When the entire-graph plugin is NOT installed, `entire-brain setup` emits **154 lines of which 142 are the host CLI's full `--help` screen**, ending with `Error: Invalid usage: unknown command "graph" for "entire"` and `Did you mean this? grant`. The real 12-line setup report is printed BELOW that wall, so a first-time user scrolls past 142 lines of noise and sees a "did you mean" that implies they mistyped something they never typed.

Two adjacent components fail from the SAME cause and report it completely differently:

- GOOD — semantic index: `semantic index failed (provider_doctor_failed: ...; the entire-graph semantic provider is not installed (entire has no `graph` command) -- install it with `entire plugin install graph`, then re-run `entire-brain setup`)`
- BAD — entity index: `entity index failed (read graph identity revision: entire [graph version --json]: exit status 1: Usage:\n  entire [flags]\n ...40+ lines of help...`

Root cause: `internal/entityindex/identity.go` lines 32 and 38 do `fmt.Errorf("read graph identity revision: %w", err)` with ZERO classification or summarisation, so the subprocess's entire stderr is embedded verbatim.

The correct behaviour already exists in `internal/cli/semantic.go` — read these two functions and mirror them exactly:
- `semanticProviderDetailSummary(detail string) string` — reduces a multi-line dump to the line marked `Error:` (first line as fallback), strips a trailing `Usage:`, caps at 200 runes with `...`.
- `semanticProviderMissing(detail string) bool` — markers: `unknown command "graph"`, `unknown command 'graph'`, `unknown command graph`, `executable file not found`, `no such file or directory`, `command not found`.
Its doc comment states the invariant you MUST preserve: **detection runs against the FULL detail, so shortening what is shown never changes what is recognised.**

1. FIRST verify the defect still exists on current `origin/main` (it was found on the #350 integration branch at 878b7dbc). Build and reproduce. If main already fixes it, STOP and report that — do not invent a fix.
   Reproduce with an isolated env so you don't touch the real brain: set `ENTIRE_BRAIN_CONFIG_DIR`, `ENTIRE_BRAIN_DATA_DIR`, `ENTIRE_BRAIN_DAEMON_DIR`, `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR`, `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR`, `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR`, `XDG_*_HOME` all under a temp dir (pointing ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR at an empty dir is what hides the graph plugin and triggers the bug), then run `<binary> setup --no-backfill --no-daemon` in a throwaway git repo with a few real commits. ALWAYS pass `--no-backfill --no-daemon`.
2. Fix at the source — `internal/entityindex/identity.go` — so all **9** `ProviderIdentity` call sites benefit (semantic.go:3216, refresh.go:771, entities_cmd.go:200/473/606/969, entities_migrate.go:20, migrate.go:130).
   - `entityindex` is a separate package and the two helpers are unexported in `internal/cli`. Pick ONE and justify it in the report: (a) small unexported mirror in `entityindex`, or (b) lift both helpers into a shared internal package and have BOTH call sites use it. (b) is better if it does not balloon the diff — two different messages for one cause is the actual bug, and duplicated logic will drift back apart.
   - PRESERVE the `read graph identity revision: ` prefix — `internal/cli/honest_reporting_fixes_test.go:212` matches on it.
   - When the detail indicates the provider is missing, say so and name the runnable remedy, matching the semantic path's wording so the two components agree.
3. Tests, each WEAKENING-VERIFIED (revert the production change, confirm RED, restore — report any guard that stays green, it is worthless):
   - a multi-line usage dump is reduced to one line
   - the missing-provider case names `entire plugin install graph`
   - detection still fires when the marker is NOT on the first line (the full-detail invariant)
   - **a class guard**: no setup component's reported failure detail exceeds N lines. This bug existed because one component was fixed and its neighbour was not — assert the property for all of them, not just entities.
4. Verify by re-running the repro: total setup output should drop from ~154 lines to roughly a dozen. Put the BEFORE and AFTER line counts in your report.
5. `go build ./... && go vet ./...`, then `go test ./internal/entityindex/ ./internal/cli/ -run 'Identity|Provider|Semantic|Entity|Detail|Honest' -count=1` with `GOMAXPROCS=1 -p 1 -parallel 1`. Do NOT run the full suite (limited cores).
6. Push the branch and open a PR against main. Conventional title in the existing style (lowercase `fix(scope): ...`). Body: the before/after line counts, the two-components-one-cause framing, and the call-site list. NO AI attribution footer, NO Co-Authored-By, NO Claude/session links.

## Hard rules
- DO NOT merge, approve, or tag. DO NOT touch `internal/cli/connect_cmd.go`, `hosted_sync.go`, `hosted_placement*.go` — another agent is editing those right now.
- Never bare `git stash`.
- `FORCE_COLOR=3` is set in this shell and breaks colour-assert tests; unset it for test runs, and if something still fails, reproduce on main before blaming your diff.
- Report honestly. If the class guard is impractical, say why instead of shipping a vacuous one.

Decisive: with a **completely clean tree (0 dirty files)**, session export still fails with the identical error and the brain is still "degraded". I did exactly what the remedy said and nothing changed — **the advice is simply wrong**. The real cause is that this repo has no captured Entire sessions at all, which is the normal state of a new repo, not a degradation.

Let me write your walkthrough:

input.command:
cat > /Users/suhaan/devenv/brain-demo/WALKTHROUGH.md <<'MD'
# Brain setup — hands-on walkthrough

A throwaway sandbox with a realistic repo. **Nothing here touches your real brain,
your real config, or your real launchd watcher** — verified, see "Safety" at the end.

## 0. One-time

```bash
source ~/devenv/brain-demo/env.sh      # isolation + `brain` shim
bash ~/devenv/brain-demo/make-repo.sh  # builds acme-payments: 13 commits, 12 files
cd "$BRAIN_DEMO_ROOT/acme-payments"
```

`env.sh` prints which binary it's using. It must say a **dev** build, not `0.1.0` —
0.1.0 is the released nightly and has none of the fixes in it.

To start over at any point: `rm -rf ~/brain-demo-sandbox && bash ~/devenv/brain-demo/make-repo.sh`

---

## 1. First run — the moment that matters most

```bash
brain setup --no-backfill --no-daemon     # spends ZERO tokens
```

Watch for: how long it takes, whether every line is something you could act on,
and whether the ending tells you what to do next.

Then the same thing as a machine would see it:

```bash
brain setup --no-backfill --no-daemon --json | python3 -m json.tool | head -40
```

## 2. What did it actually build?

```bash
brain status                  # coverage, freshness, onboarding progress
brain status --verbose        # the full report
brain doctor                  # 24 ok / 3 warn / 1 error, each with a remedy
brain stats                   # record counts by kind
```

**Try every remedy either command prints.** They are supposed to be runnable
verbatim. Note any that aren't, or that don't change anything.

## 3. Use the brain

```bash
brain overview                              # what is this project?
brain brief "add idempotency keys to payments"
brain query "why are payments held instead of rejected"
brain query "where is the overdraft rule enforced"
brain inspect search-graph --query "Transfer"
brain entities --symbol Transfer
brain dash                                  # interactive TUI — needs a real terminal
```

`overview` and `brief` are the two an agent hits first. The mock repo has a
deliberate architectural decision recorded in `docs/architecture.md` ("held, not
rejected") — a good brain should surface it for the `query` above.

## 4. Durable facts

```bash
brain remember "Balances are folds over the entry log, never stored" --path architecture.ledger.invariant
brain recall "balance"
brain facts
brain verify
```

Facts are **branch-scoped** — `recall` on a different branch comes back empty.
Worth seeing for yourself:

```bash
git switch -c experiment && brain recall "balance"   # empty
git switch main          && brain recall "balance"   # there
```

## 5. The background watcher

cat > /Users/suhaan/devenv/brain-demo/FINDINGS.md <<'MD'
# First-run defects found by actually running setup

Measured in an isolated sandbox against a dev build of the #350 integration
branch (878b7dbc), on a realistic repo (13 commits, 12 files).

## 1. Without the graph plugin, setup emits 142 lines of someone else's help text

`setup` → **154 lines, of which 142 are the host CLI's full `--help` screen**,
signed off with `Error: Invalid usage: unknown command "graph"` and
`Did you mean this? grant`. The real 12-line report prints *below* the wall, so a
first-time user scrolls past 142 lines of noise and is told they mistyped a
command they never typed. With the plugin present the same run is 35 lines.

Two components fail from the **same cause** and report it completely differently:

- semantic index → `the entire-graph semantic provider is not installed (entire has no 'graph' command) -- install it with 'entire plugin install graph', then re-run 'entire-brain setup'` ✅
- entity index → `read graph identity revision: entire [graph version --json]: exit status 1: Usage:` + 40 lines ❌

Root cause: `internal/entityindex/identity.go:32,38` wrap the subprocess error
with no summarisation. `internal/cli/semantic.go` already has the right
machinery (`semanticProviderDetailSummary`, `semanticProviderMissing`) — the
entity path never got it. 9 call sites of `ProviderIdentity` are affected.
**Fix in flight.**

## 2. The remedy for the one error does not work

Fresh repo → `Brain ready (degraded)`, and `status` says:

> sessions failed, freshness degraded -- **commit or stash the working tree** -- or
> list the paths in .brainignore ... then re-run `entire-brain setup`

Tested: committed everything, confirmed `git status --porcelain` = **0 files**,
re-ran setup. **Identical failure, still degraded.** The advice is wrong.

Worse, the 4 files that dirty the tree on a first run — `.claude/`, `.entire/`,
`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` — are **created by setup itself**. So setup dirties the
tree and then tells the user to clean up after it.

The actual cause is that the repo has no captured Entire sessions, which is the
**normal** state of a new repo. Calling it "degraded" and emitting
`no_egress: a complete readable local checkpoint catalog could not be
established; refusing routed checkpoint discovery` reads as a malfunction.

## 3. setup and doctor refer the user to each other

- `setup` → "run 'entire-brain doctor' for detail"
- `doctor` → "setup session export: error (...; run `entire-brain setup`)"

A first-time user bounces between the two and neither resolves it.

## 4. The version-skew remedy points the wrong way

> semantic provider emitted schema_version "1.3" but this build reads 1.1 ...
> **upgrade entire-brain** to ingest everything "1.3" carries

`doctor`'s remedy for that same condition is `entire plugin install graph` —
upgrading the component that is already *ahead*. The message and its remedy
disagree about which side is behind.

## 5. Unknown subcommands exit 0 and print parent help

`entire-brain entities lookup` (not a real subcommand) prints the parent help and
exits 0 rather than erroring. Makes typos silent, and makes "I ran --help on all
95 documented commands" a weaker check than it sounds.

---

## What is genuinely good

- The daemon pre-install warning names the path, says it restarts at every
  login, and gives both escape hatches **before** installing.
- Daemon isolation works: label is scoped by a hash of the unit dir
  (`io.entire.brain-watch.a2d3fd66.10affb60` vs the real `...a2d3fd66`). Both ran
  side by side; `--uninstall-daemon` removed only the sandbox one.
- `status` says `0/0 distilled (no captured sessions yet)` — honest and clear.
- `doctor` gives `24 ok, 3 warn, 1 error` with a remedy per line.
- `entities history Transfer` correctly returns the method and its test with commits.
- Instant phase: ~1s, genuinely zero token spend.

content.text:
Everything's in place. Here's where it all landed.

## Your PRs

**#340 is fixed** — rebased, head `2eb20bbb`, MERGEABLE. It turned out main had done more than rename the command: it also renamed `resolveWhereami` → `resolveHostedPlacement`, which collided with #340's *cached wrapper* of the same name. That's now split cleanly (`cachedHostedPlacement` for the cached path). Zero `whereami` strings left, all 6 weakenings fire, 80 tests pass.

**#350 is updated** (`878b7dbc..f6834163`) but it introduced the regression I flagged — in resolving conflicts it took main's connect text and silently reverted #340's whole point. Re-integration is running now. Worth noting it merged rather than rebased (a true rebase replayed 53 commits); the tree is right, the history isn't linear.

## Your setup sandbox

```bash
source ~/devenv/brain-demo/env.sh
bash ~/devenv/brain-demo/make-repo.sh
cd "$BRAIN_DEMO_ROOT/acme-payments"
brain setup --no-backfill --no-daemon
```

Full sequence in `~/devenv/brain-demo/WALKTHROUGH.md` — every command in it I ran first. Three of my own were wrong (`--symbol`, `--query`, `--dry-run` don't exist) and are corrected; `brain dash` is the only one I couldn't verify, since a TUI can't be judged through a pipe.

The repo is a real one — `acme-payments`, 13 commits, a ledger/risk/gateway split with a recorded architectural decision in its docs, so `query` and `brief` have something real to find.

**Isolation is proven, not assumed.** The sandbox watcher installs as `io.entire.brain-watch.a2d3fd66.10affb60`; yours is `io.entire.brain-watch.a2d3fd66`. Both ran side by side, and `--uninstall-daemon` removed only the sandbox one — your pid 5190 never moved. One honest gap: the session-end hook lives in `~/.claude/settings.json`, which no isolation variable governs. It was already wired here so setup only read it.

## What running it actually found

Five defects, in `~/devenv/brain-demo/FINDINGS.md`. Two matter a lot:

**Without the graph plugin, setup prints 142 lines of the host CLI's help screen** — 92% of its output — and signs off `Did you mean this? grant`, so a new user is told they mistyped a command they never typed. The real report is buried underneath. With the plugin it's 35 lines. The damning part: the semantic index handles the *identical* failure perfectly (`install it with 'entire plugin install graph'`) while the entity index five lines later dumps raw stderr. `semantic.go` already has the machinery; `entityindex` never got it. Fix is in flight.

**The one error's remedy does not work.** A fresh repo reports `Brain ready (degraded)` and tells you to "commit or stash the working tree". I did exactly that — confirmed `git status --porcelain` empty — re-ran, and got the identical failure. And the files dirtying the tree (`.claude/`, `.entire/`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`) are the ones **setup just created**. The real cause is simply that a new repo has no captured sessions, which is normal, not degraded.

Plus: `setup` → "run doctor", `doctor` → "run setup" (a closed loop); the version-skew message says upgrade entire-brain while doctor's remedy says upgrade graph, which is the side already ahead; and unknown subcommands exit 0 printing parent help.

Genuinely good: the daemon pre-install warning names the path, the login persistence and both escape hatches *before* acting. That one's a model for the rest.

Two agents still running — the entity-index fix and the #350 re-integration. Nothing merged, nothing tagged.

Good work on #372 — the class guard across 11 components × 4 render sites is exactly right, and catching that Flatten must not cap an already-short detail is a good call.

Two follow-ups on the same PR. Both are things I verified live just now, so treat them as ground truth.

## 1. Your wording deviation picked the wrong side — please switch it

You matched main's `install it with \`scripts/install.sh\` from the entire-brain checkout`. That remedy is NOT runnable for an end user: it assumes they have the entire-brain source checkout. Most users installing the plugin do not.

VERIFIED LIVE just now:
```
$ entire plugin search graph
* graph   Deterministic local code graph for symbol search, relationship tracing, and change-impact analysis [official]
* = installed. Install with 'entire plugin install <name>'.
```
`graph` is in the official plugin index and `entire plugin install graph` is the correct, runnable form. The #350 branch already uses it (`semantic.go:1250`, `:1252`, `:1324`) — it is part of the "make printed advice runnable" fix stack. main simply has not caught up.

Change `providerdetail.MissingRemedy` to the `entire plugin install graph` form. Keep your agreement test — the point is that both components agree AND the thing they agree on actually works. Note in the PR body that this intentionally diverges from main's current wording because main's is not runnable, so the reviewer sees it was deliberate.

## 2. Same PR: the version-skew remedy points at the wrong component

Separate condition, same subsystem, and it is the mirror image of the bug you just fixed — a message and its remedy disagreeing.

- `internal/cli/semantic.go:1804` says: `semantic provider emitted schema_version %q but this build reads %s; minors are additive, so the snapshot is usable, but upgrade **entire-brain** to ingest everything %q carries`
- `internal/cli/doctor.go:696` has a STATIC per-component remedy: `"semantic provider": "entire plugin install graph"`

So on a version-skew warning, doctor tells the user to install/upgrade **graph** — the side that is already ahead. Doing it cannot help, and may widen the skew.

Observed verbatim:
```
semantic provider: warn (provider=degraded (semantic provider emitted schema_version "1.3" but this build reads 1.1; minors are additive, so the snapshot is usable, but upgrade entire-b…; run `entire plugin install graph`)
```

Root cause is structural: the remedy is a static map keyed by component name, so it cannot vary by condition. Make the semantic-provider remedy condition-dependent — provider-missing → install graph; provider-ahead/version-skew → upgrade entire-brain. If other entries in that map have the same latent problem, say so in your report rather than fixing them all.

## Tests
Weakening-verify both, as before. For #2, the valuable guard is the property, not the string: **a remedy must name the component the message says is behind**. Assert that for both conditions, so the two can never disagree again.

## Constraints unchanged
Do NOT touch `internal/cli/connect_cmd.go`, `hosted_sync.go`, `hosted_placement*.go` — another agent is in `internal/cli/status_render.go` and `setup.go` right now, so if your change needs either of those, stop and report instead of editing. Do not merge/approve/tag. No AI attribution footer. Push to the same branch so #372 updates.

Report: what changed, weakening results, and the before/after doctor line for the skew case.

```
no_egress: a complete readable local checkpoint catalog could not be established

x sessions failed, freshness degraded -- run `entire-brain refresh --agent none`
```

the remedy cannot fix it and re-emits itself; and the correct message already

"""

cat > /Users/suhaan/devenv/brain-demo/SETUP-REDESIGN.md <<'MD'
# `entire brain setup` — redesign spec

## Why

The machinery is fine (`refreshProgress` phases, `liveTerminal` repaints, TTY-gated
`tui.Render`). The problem is volume and redundancy. On a TTY today:

```
⠹ ✗✓✓✓ instant core: doc index              <- 9 sub-components as a cryptic tick-run
⠹ ✗✓✓✓✓✓✓ instant core: pattern layer
✓ instant core ready in 300ms — built seed, history, docs, semantic, fact… done
  session export failed (no_egress: a complete readable local checkpoint …)
− pre-edit hook already wired (…/.claude/settings.json) skipped
− fact backfill (--no-backfill) skipped
…
  instant     ✗ session export ✓ seed baseline ✓ history index ✓ doc index …   <- ALL 9 AGAIN
```

The same nine components are rendered three times: inline in the spinner, in the
completion sentence, and again in the summary. `setup.go` is 1928 lines with 37
progress call sites.

Token spend is also opt-OUT (`--no-backfill`). A first run distills without asking.

## Target

### Seven phases, one line each while running, one line each when done

| # | phase | what it covers |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Detect** | repo, git state, agent CLI, model + effort, graph provider, hosted binding |
| 2 | **Build** | the whole instant core — 9 components behind ONE progress bar |
| 3 | **Agents** | agent instructions + pre-edit hook + session-end hook |
| 4 | **Facts** | **asks before spending**; then distills |
| 5 | **Workspace** | registration |
| 6 | **Watcher** | daemon (keep today's excellent pre-install warning verbatim) |
| 7 | **Ready** | verdict + next steps |

Sub-components report *into* their phase's bar, never as their own top-level line.
A failure promotes exactly one line beneath its phase — never a stderr dump
(that invariant is already enforced by `providerdetail.Flatten`).

### The summary block stops repeating the phases

Today it re-lists every component. It should show only what the phase lines could
not: paths (repo, brain), the verdict, and any failure's one-line reason.

### Ask before spending tokens

Phase 4 prompts when, and only when, there is something to spend on:

```
  Facts   12 sessions can be distilled into durable facts.
          Agent: claude-code · model: claude-haiku-5-5 · effort: low
          Estimated: ~12 agent calls, newest first, resumable.

          Distill now? [y/N]
```

- Default **No**. Enter = skip. Never spend on silence.
- Skipped → the brain is still fully queryable; print the one command that starts it later.
- **Non-interactive (no TTY, CI, piped) must never block**: no prompt, default No, say so in one line.
- `--yes` / `--no-backfill` keep working and suppress the prompt. `--yes` is the
  only way to spend without a human.
- Do not prompt when there is nothing to distill (0 sessions) or no agent CLI.

### Show model and provider capabilities

Phase 1 prints what was detected, so the Facts prompt is an informed decision:

```
  Detect  repo acme-payments · 13 commits · clean tree
          agent    claude-code (claude-haiku-5-5, effort low)
          provider entire-graph v0.4.1   semantic ✓  entities ✓
          hosted   not bound — local-only (COR-2029)
```

Each line states a real capability. Anything unavailable says so and names its
one-line remedy. No line that cannot be acted on.

### Colour

Per-phase accent carried by `tui.Phase`; state colour on the glyph
(running / ok / skipped / failed). Must degrade correctly for `NO_COLOR`, a
non-UTF-8 locale, and a pipe — those are four distinct cases and
`newProgressWithRenderer` already separates them. Do not hand-roll ANSI; go
through `tui.Render`.

## Non-negotiables

- `setup` still exits 0 whenever the brain is queryable; non-zero only when nothing usable exists.
- Re-running stays safe and resumes rather than restarts.
- No phase may spend a token before phase 4's consent.
- Every printed command must be runnable verbatim.
- Behaviour identical under a pipe, minus the repaints.
MD

Spec is at `~/devenv/brain-demo/SETUP-REDESIGN.md`. I think I've got your complaint exactly: `⠹ ✗✓✓✓✓✓✓ instant core: pattern layer` reads like pytest's `....F..` — a test-runner tick-run, not a setup experience. That's the thing to kill.

**Ready to test right now** — four fixes landed and are in the sandbox binary:

```bash
bash ~/devenv/brain-demo/rebuild.sh      # already at 024e2923
source ~/devenv/brain-demo/env.sh
cd "$BRAIN_DEMO_ROOT/acme-payments"
brain setup --no-backfill --no-daemon
```

| | |
|---|---|
| #340 | rebased, truth-telling restored, 0 `whereami` left, 6/6 weakenings fire |
| #350 | #340 re-integrated; the "binding automatically" lie verified **gone** |
| docs | getting-started + reference no longer promise auto-binding |
| #372 | **new PR** — entity-index dump 168 → 52 lines, class guard over 11 components × 4 render sites |

Two corrections to my earlier findings, since you'd otherwise test against a wrong list: the "commit or stash" remedy was **not** wrong (correctly gated on a genuinely dirty tree), and unknown subcommands do **not** exit 0 — that was `--help` doing normal cobra things. `FINDINGS.md` is updated.

**The redesign — 7 phases, consent prompt, capability display, colour**

The real find from the PTY capture: the machinery is already good. You have spinners, phases, a progress bar and TTY gating. The problem is that nine instant components render *three times* — as the tick-run, in the completion sentence, and again in the summary block.

Shape I'm building to: Detect → Build → Agents → Facts → Workspace → Watcher → Ready. Nine components collapse behind one bar in **Build**. **Detect** prints agent, model, effort and provider capability so the next prompt is informed. **Facts** asks `Distill now? [y/N]` — default No, never spends on silence, never blocks without a TTY, and only asks when there's actually something to spend on. `--yes` becomes the only way to spend unattended.

Two calls I made rather than asking: consent gates *any* token spend, not just backfill; and non-interactive always defaults to not spending. Say the word if you'd rather have either the other way.

It's queued, not started — the no-sessions loop fix is still editing `setup.go` and I won't have two agents in a 1928-line file. I'll start the moment it lands and ping you when the redesign is testable.

Caught myself again — there **is** a verdict, it just adapts:

```
Brain set up, but not queryable in 300ms
  no semantic index and no seed baseline -- `entire-brain query` and `entire-brain brief` have nothing to read for this repo yet
```

That's honest and good. My grep assumed one fixed string. But it exposes a genuine contract violation:

input.command:
cat >> /Users/suhaan/devenv/brain-demo/FINDINGS.md <<'MD'

---

# Edge-case sweep (8 repo shapes)

| case | exit | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| empty repo, no commits | 0 | Brain ready (degraded) |
| **not a git repo** | 1 | **exemplary — see below** |
| dirty worktree | 0 | Brain set up, but not queryable |
| detached HEAD | 0 | Brain ready (degraded) |
| binary-only repo | 0 | Brain ready (degraded) |
| path with spaces | 0 | Brain ready (degraded) |
| unicode path (репо-名前) | 0 | Brain ready (degraded) |
| read-only repo dir | 0 | Brain ready (degraded) |

No crashes, no hangs. Paths with spaces and unicode are handled correctly.

## 8. `not a git repository` is the model every other message should copy

```
not a git repository: /path/to/notgit
entire-brain setup builds every source it has -- sessions, seed, docs, semantic
index, entities -- from git history, so it needs git and a repository.
run `git init` here and make at least one commit, or name a repository:
entire-brain setup <path>
```
What is wrong, why it matters, and two runnable ways out — in three lines.
Use this as the template for the redesign.

## 9. The exit-code contract contradicts itself

`setup --help` states: *"setup exits 0 whenever the brain is queryable — that is,
whenever at least one instant-phase component built."*

Those two clauses are not the same thing. On a dirty worktree, 3 of 7 components
build (docs, entities, memory) so the proxy says exit 0 — while the product
itself prints **"Brain set up, but not queryable"**. A script doing
`entire-brain setup && entire-brain query ...` proceeds on a brain that cannot
answer.

Fix the contract, not the message: exit non-zero when the brain is not queryable,
or stop calling exit 0 "queryable".

## NOT defects — tested and withdrawn

- **Setup does not compound its own dirt.** It writes `.claude/`, `.entire/`,
  `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, but the seed/index gates exempt them — a second run
  on an uncommitted tree still builds everything. Verified by running setup twice
  and committing nothing.
- **The verdict line is not missing on the dirty path.** It changes text by state
  ("Brain set up, but not queryable" instead of "Brain ready"). My grep assumed a
  fixed string.

input.message:
Extra requirement for the setupui work, with a measurement behind it.

## Terminal width is currently unhandled — make it a hard constraint

I measured today's output under a real PTY at forced widths:

```
width 40: longest rendered line = 202 chars  -> OVERFLOWS (5x)
width 60: longest rendered line = 202 chars  -> OVERFLOWS (3.4x)
```

The offender is the summary line you are already deleting:
`  instant     ✗ session export  ✓ seed baseline  ✓ history index  ✓ doc index  ✓ semantic index  ✓ pattern layer  ✓ entity index  ✓ memory coordinator  (340ms)`

It is emitted at a fixed 202 chars regardless of terminal width, so it wraps into unreadable mush on any normal split pane.

### Requirements
- NO line the new UI emits may exceed the terminal width. Detect width from the TTY; fall back to 80 when unknown (pipe, no winsize).
- Truncate or re-flow rather than wrap. If you truncate, do it on a word/segment boundary with an ellipsis, never mid-escape-sequence and never mid-multibyte-rune — `репо-名前` paths and `✓`/`⠋` glyphs are all in play (I verified unicode paths reach this code).
- The progress bar must size itself to the available width, not a constant.
- Respect `COLUMNS` when set, since that is how people test this.

### Test it for real
Add a width test that renders at **40, 60, 80 and 200 columns** and asserts no emitted line exceeds the width. Weakening-verify it: hardcode a 202-char line and confirm the test goes RED at 40 and 80.

For the PTY harness, `script` does NOT work in this environment (`tcgetattr/ioctl: Operation not supported on socket`). Use Python's `pty.fork()` plus `fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", rows, cols, 0, 0))` — that is what I used and it works. Strip ANSI with `s/\x1b\[[0-9;?]*[a-zA-Z]//g` and convert `\r` to newline before measuring, or you will measure the repaint stream rather than the rendered frame.

## Two more things I verified that you can rely on
- Interrupting setup mid-run (SIGINT) leaves no corruption; the next run recovers cleanly. Don't add recovery scaffolding for a problem that doesn't exist.
- Two concurrent `setup` runs both exit 0 with no lock error. Your UI must not assume it is the only writer, but it also need not serialise anything.

Everything else in the original brief stands, including the file boundary — still do not touch `setup.go`, `status_render.go`, `semantic.go`, `doctor.go`, `connect_cmd.go`, `hosted_*`.

Groundwork for the redesign is done while the two builds run. Where things stand:

**Specs written** (both in `~/devenv/brain-demo/`):
- `SETUP-REDESIGN.md` — the 7 phases, the consent prompt, the capability block, colour rules
- `INTEGRATION-MAP.md` — all **40** `setup.go` call sites mapped to phases, so wiring is mechanical

The collapse is bigger than I first thought. Facts alone has **nine** separate skip variants, each printing its own top-level line (`fact backfill (--no-backfill)`, `: no captured sessions yet`, `: already complete`, `: no agent CLI on PATH`…). The watcher has nine more. Every one is a legitimate *reason* — none deserves its own line. That's where your "too complicated" comes from.

**Edge-case sweep — 8 repo shapes, plus robustness:**

| verified broken | verified fine |
|---|---|
| 202-char line, **ignores terminal width** (5× overflow at 40 cols) | SIGINT mid-run → clean recovery |
| exit-code contract self-contradicts (§9) | two concurrent setups → both exit 0, no corruption |
| | spaces + unicode paths (`репо-名前`) |
| | empty repo, detached HEAD, binary-only, read-only dir, git worktree |

The width bug I sent straight to the UI agent with the measurement and a PTY harness that works here (`script` can't allocate a terminal in this environment — `pty.fork()` + `TIOCSWINSZ` can).

Also captured `json-baseline.json` (schema_version 1) so I can prove the redesign doesn't move the machine-readable contract — `--json` must survive untouched.

**Best thing I found:** `not a git repository` already does it right — what's wrong, why it matters, two runnable fixes, three lines. I've made that the template rather than inventing a new voice.

Still building: the `setupui` package (7-phase renderer, capability block, consent prompt, four render modes) and the no-sessions fix that currently owns `setup.go`. I'll wire them together and ping you when it's testable.

Good work, and thank you for the scope correction — you were right and I was wrong. I independently reproduced it: with `ENTIRE_BRAIN_LOCAL_ONLY=1` session export fails and every run reads "Brain ready (degraded)"; with it unset the same repo and binary build all nine components and report plain "Brain ready". My sandbox set that rail, so I manufactured the trigger I then reported. I have made it opt-in. Catching that mattered.

Two things, both small.

## 1. Amend out the Co-Authored-By trailer

Please do. `devenv/CLAUDE.md` says "No AI attribution footers in commits", and the harness reminder that mandates the trailer explicitly defers: "the user's own instructions about these lines, such as a CLAUDE.md or memory rule, take precedence over this reminder". So CLAUDE.md wins. Amend it off every commit on `fix/brain-nosessions-loop` and force-push with `--force-with-lease`. The user has asked for this repeatedly, so it is not a style nit.

## 2. Confirm the loop guard survives egress being ALLOWED

Your own correction raises this. The `no_egress` trigger was sandbox-induced, but you kept faults 2 and 3 (misclassification + self-referential remedy) as applying to the egress-allowed `checkpoint_scope_incomplete` path too. I want that nailed down rather than assumed, because it is now the only version of this bug a real user can hit.

Please confirm, with a transcript, that on a repo with **no captured sessions and egress ALLOWED** (no `ENTIRE_BRAIN_LOCAL_ONLY`, no `ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS`):
- the sessions component is not reported as failed
- the verdict is not "degraded" for that reason alone
- no status/doctor next-step re-emits itself
- your new `firstrun_no_sessions_test.go` guards cover that path and not only the no-egress one

If any guard only exercises the no-egress path, extend it — otherwise the fix is tested for a configuration real users do not run. If they already cover both, say so explicitly and paste the egress-allowed transcript.

Nothing else changes. Do not merge, approve or tag. Same file boundaries as before.

input.message:
Two corrections and one concrete design target. All measured, all after fixing a flaw in my own sandbox.

## Correction: ignore any "degraded" you saw in my earlier material

My sandbox set `ENTIRE_BRAIN_LOCAL_ONLY=1` as a safety rail, and that alone makes session export refuse (`no_egress: ...`), turning every run into "Brain ready (degraded)". Same repo, same binary, rail removed: all nine components build and it reports plain `Brain ready`. The rail manufactured the symptom. `~/devenv/brain-demo/env.sh` no longer sets it.

Corrected baseline for the healthy path: **33 lines**, verdict `Brain ready`.

## The design target — 47 lines vs 2, same program

This contrast is the whole brief in one pair of numbers.

A repo with **no commits yet**:
- **47 lines**, three component failures (seed baseline, semantic index, entity index), verdict `Brain set up, but not queryable`.

A directory that is **not a git repo at all**:
```
not a git repository: /path/to/notgit
entire-brain setup builds every source it has -- sessions, seed, docs, semantic
index, entities -- from git history, so it needs git and a repository.
run `git init` here and make at least one commit, or name a repository:
entire-brain setup <path>
```
- **2 lines** (plus wrap). What is wrong, why it matters, two runnable ways out. Exit 1.

Same class of problem — "this repo has nothing to index yet" — and 23x the output for the easier case. The no-commits path should read much closer to the second: state the condition once, name the one action, stop. It should NOT render three red component failures, because nothing is broken.

**Make this a test case.** A repo with zero commits must produce a short, single-reason result, not a failure list. Assert a line-count ceiling for it (pick a defensible number and justify it) and weakening-verify by restoring the per-component failure rendering.

More generally: a phase whose inputs do not exist yet is **not** a failure. Expected-empty and broken must render differently — that distinction is the core of the redesign, and PR #373 (now open) establishes it for the sessions component specifically. Read that diff if it helps; do not duplicate it.

## Corrected edge-case baseline you can design against

| case | exit | lines | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| empty repo, no commits | 0 | 47 | Brain set up, but not queryable |
| not a git repo | 1 | 2 | (exemplary) |
| dirty worktree | 0 | 41 | Brain set up, but not queryable |
| detached HEAD / binary-only / spaces / unicode / read-only | 0 | 32-33 | Brain ready |

No crashes or hangs anywhere, including unicode paths (`репо-名前`) and paths with spaces, so handle those as working input rather than hazards.

Everything else in the brief stands, including the file boundary. `setup.go` is now free — but it is MINE to wire; keep building standalone packages.

Material correction you should have before you test anything.

**My sandbox was manufacturing the bug I kept reporting.** `env.sh` set `ENTIRE_BRAIN_LOCAL_ONLY=1` as a network safety rail. That alone makes session export refuse, which is what turned *every* run into "Brain ready (degraded)". Same repo, same binary, rail removed:

```
LOCAL_ONLY=1   → session export failed (no_egress…)  → Brain ready (degraded)
LOCAL_ONLY off → all nine components built            → Brain ready
```

The subagent caught it, I reproduced it both ways, and the sandbox now leaves it unset (opt in with `BRAIN_DEMO_NO_EGRESS=1`). The honest healthy baseline is **33 lines, `Brain ready`** — not the degraded mess I showed you earlier. The *reporting* faults survive the correction, because they also fire on the normal egress-allowed path.

That's three of my findings now corrected by testing them. The edge-case table is re-run and `FINDINGS.md` carries the corrections rather than quietly dropping them.

**The sharpest result from the clean sweep** — same program, same class of problem:

| case | lines |
|---|---|
| repo with **no commits** | **47**, three red component failures |
| directory that is **not a git repo** | **2**, and it's excellent |

23× the output for the easier case. A phase whose inputs don't exist yet is not a failure — that distinction is now the core of the redesign, and it's a test case with a line-count ceiling.

**PR #373** is open — the no-sessions fix. It found a third loop site I'd missed (doctor's `capture` check recommends a refresh that succeeds while still exporting zero, so it re-prints forever), and all ten weakenings fire including two deliberate over-fixes. 528 tests pass. I've asked it to strip the `Co-Authored-By` trailer CLAUDE.md forbids, and to prove its guards cover the egress-allowed path rather than only the configuration my sandbox created.

Open now: **#341** (doctor remedy direction — my cite was off by a branch, it lives there not on main), **#372** (entity-index, 168→52 lines), **#373**.

Still building: the `setupui` package. `setup.go` is free now, so the wiring is mine to do the moment it lands.

- **Three hooks I added to `internal/cli/progress.go` for exactly this job** (commit `9b4140f3`, tested in `progress_hooks_test.go`):
  - `(*refreshProgress).TTY() bool`
  - `(*refreshProgress).EmitLine(string)` — writes a composed line verbatim, through the live terminal
  - `(*refreshProgressTask).Abandon()` — ends the live row and writes NOTHING (the third outcome Finish cannot express)

Use them. Note the semantics I verified while building them: **plain mode announces a task at `Begin` on purpose** (so a log reads in event order) — `Abandon` cannot un-write that and must not try. `Finish(nil)` is deliberately silent when the label is unchanged since Begin; a failure always prints.

## The job
Route setup's existing reporting into the 7 phases: Detect, Build, Agents, Facts, Workspace, Watcher, Ready. One line per phase. Sub-steps feed their phase's bar and never emit a top-level line.

Biggest collapses (from the map):
- **Build**: 9 instant components → ONE line + bar. Kills the `⠹ ✗✓✓✓✓✓✓ instant core: pattern layer` tick-run, which reads like pytest output. This is the single most important change.
- **Facts**: 9 `progress.Skip("fact backfill: …")` variants at setup.go ~1022-1062 → ONE line carrying the reason.
- **Watcher**: 9 variants (~830-998) → ONE line. **Keep the pre-install warning text verbatim** — it names the path, says it restarts at every login, and gives both escape hatches. It is the best text in the command.
- **Ready**: summary stops re-listing the phases; it shows only paths, verdict, failure reasons, next steps.

1. **Consent before token spend.** Add a `--yes` flag. Wire `setupui.Consent` into the Facts phase: prompt only when there is something to spend on; default No; `--yes` → spend, `--no-backfill` → skip, both suppress the prompt; **never block without a TTY**.
2. **Detect phase** — fill `setupui.Detected` from what setup already resolves (repo facts, agent/model/effort, graph provider capability, hosted binding). The renderer takes a struct; do the detection in `setup.go`.
3. **Fix the exit-code contract.** `setup --help` claims "exits 0 whenever the brain is queryable — that is, whenever at least one instant-phase component built". Those two clauses disagree: on a dirty worktree 3 of 7 components build, so it exits 0 while printing **"Brain set up, but not queryable"**. Make exit status follow *queryable*, and update the help text to match. A script doing `setup && query` must not proceed on a brain that cannot answer.
4. **Zero-commit repo** must render short (setupui has a 10-line ceiling test for it), not as three red component failures. Nothing is broken; there is just nothing to index.

- `--no-backfill`, `--no-daemon`, `--uninstall-daemon`, `--workspace`, `--interval`, `--distill-every`, `--agent`, `--model`, `--effort`, `--backfill-budget` semantics.
- Re-running stays safe and resumable. Interrupt (SIGINT) and two concurrent runs both work today — verified — and must still.

Confirmed — a real bug, and a nasty one:

```
\x1b[38;5;203m█\x1b[0m   ×6   ← fine
\x1b[3…\x1b[0m            ← truncated MID-ESCAPE
```

The cut landed inside `\x1b[38;5;203m`, leaving a dangling `\x1b[3` before the ellipsis. A terminal seeing an incomplete CSI swallows whatever follows. The width test couldn't catch it because it measures *after* stripping ANSI — the stripped length was fine; the cut position wasn't. And it only happens on the live bar row, so no pipe test would ever see it.

content.text: My implementation was wrong and the tests caught it instantly. The bug: `[` is `0x5B`, which is inside my "final byte" range `0x40–0x7e`, so the scanner stopped at the `[` and treated `38;5;45m` as visible text. A CSI is `ESC [ params intermediates final` — the parameters must be skipped first:

lines: // Copy the whole sequence or none of it; never a prefix.
// Track whether a colour is left open, so the cut can close it.
+// skipANSI returns the index just past the escape sequence starting at i.
+// 0x40-0x7e>. The '[' must be stepped over BEFORE hunting the final byte:
+// 0x5b is itself inside the final-byte range, so a scanner that does not
+// will stop on the bracket and read the parameters as visible text. That is
+// not hypothetical — it is the bug the first draft of this function shipped,
+// which measured "\x1b[38;5;45m" as eight visible cells.
// isANSIFinalByte reports the byte that ends a CSI sequence (@ through ~).
func isANSIFinalByte(b byte) bool { return b >= 0x40 && b <= 0x7e }

Everything you asked for is in: seven phases, a real spinner and sized progress bar per phase, `Distill now? [y/N]` defaulting to No and never reading stdin without a TTY, the Detect block naming agent/model/effort and provider capability, and colour that never carries meaning alone.

**I found a bug in it before you could.** The live bar was truncating *mid-ANSI-escape* — `\x1b[3…` with no final byte, which makes a terminal swallow whatever comes next. The width test couldn't see it because it measures after stripping escapes; the length was fine, the cut position wasn't. `TruncateTo` now measures visible cells, never cuts inside a sequence, and closes a colour it cuts through. A PTY capture carried **3 partial sequences before, 0 after** — and I ran the detector against the pre-fix capture first, so that zero means something.

My own first fix was also wrong, and the tests caught it in one run: `[` is `0x5B`, which sits inside the CSI final-byte range, so my scanner stopped at the bracket and read `38;5;45m` as visible text. The parameters have to be skipped first.

Two judgement calls worth your eye. A **zero-commit repo now exits 1** — defensible (nothing is queryable, and the sibling not-a-git-repo case exits 1 too) but it's a behaviour change that could trip a script doing `setup && …`. And in `--json`, no key moved and `schema_version` stays 1, but `backfill.detail` now carries the consent reason rather than the bare flag name.

`internal/cli` is green except `TestOllamaDistillAgentEnvelopeAllowanceIsCeilinged`, the load-flake I root-caused in #351, which isn't on this branch.

import os,pty,sys,struct,fcntl,termios,re,subprocess
BIN=os.environ["BRAIN_BIN"]; REPO=sys.argv[1]
def pty_run(cols, env_extra):
    env=dict(os.environ); env.update(env_extra)
    out=[]
    pid,fd=pty.fork()
    if pid==0:
        os.chdir(REPO)
        for k,v in env_extra.items(): os.environ[k]=v

    try:
        while True:
            d=os.read(fd,4096)
            if not d: break
            out.append(d)
    except OSError: pass
    os.waitpid(pid,0)
    return b"".join(out)

  separately reports the 268-session backlog.

| case | lines | exit | verdict |

recovers, two concurrent setups both succeed, git worktree checkouts work.

| mode | colour | glyphs | lines over width | partial escapes |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| 40 cols | yes | unicode | 0 | 0 |
| 60 cols | yes | unicode | 0 | 0 |
| 200 cols | yes | unicode | 0 | 0 |

## 4. The mid-escape truncation bug I found and fixed

`TruncateTo` measured with runewidth, which charges an escape's bytes as cells
and cuts through the middle of one. Live capture of the progress bar:

```
                                    ^^^^^ cut mid-sequence
```

A terminal handed `ESC [ 3` with no final byte waits for the rest and swallows
what follows. Fixed: truncate by VISIBLE cells, never cut inside a sequence,
close a colour the cut opens.

```

AFTER  fix   partial escapes=0  bytes=3274
```

My own first fix was also wrong: `[` is 0x5B, inside the CSI final-byte range,
so the scanner stopped at the bracket and read `38;5;45m` as visible text. The
tests caught it on the first run.

`TestOllamaDistillAgentEnvelopeAllowanceIsCeilinged` failed on `feat/setup-ui`.
Run on **unmodified `origin/main` (c6e10f81)**, three times: **exit 1, 0, 1** —
`read 40894464 bytes`, matching the recorded root cause. Pre-existing and flaky
on main, not caused by the UI branch.

It is NOT flaky on the integration branch: #351's fix is already there and the
test passes 3/3. `feat/setup-ui` branches off main, which is why it saw it.

**The consent prompt now runs for real**, on a TTY, against 268 genuine sessions, both answers:

```
  Facts     1 session can be distilled into durable facts.
            Agent: claude-code · effort: low
            Estimated: ~1 agent call, newest first, resumable.
            Distill now? [y/N]
```

`n` → nothing starts (stub log shows one `--version` call, so declining spends nothing). `y` → backfill starts. Piped stdin → *"no terminal to ask, and silence is not consent"*, no block, no spend.

**Two real bugs I found by running it rather than reading it.**

The live bar was truncating **mid-ANSI-escape** — `\x1b[3` with no final byte, which makes a terminal swallow the next characters. The width test couldn't see it because it measures after stripping escapes. Negative control: **3 partial sequences before the fix, 0 after**. My own first fix was wrong too — `[` is `0x5B`, inside the CSI final-byte range, so my scanner stopped at the bracket; the tests caught it in one run.

And a truth-telling wart of exactly the kind this whole effort is about: a bare re-run said `not distilled (--no-backfill)` to someone who typed no such flag. `resolveSetupToggle` folds "typed" and "remembered" into one boolean, so the message blamed a flag that was never passed and never mentioned `--backfill`, the only way back. It now says *"you declined on an earlier run; --backfill starts it"*.

I also caught an uncommitted edit sitting in the merge worktree that would have dropped `--backfill` from the consent set — meaning that flag would silently do nothing in the unattended runs it exists for. Reverted, and pinned with a test that goes red on exactly that edit.

Evidence is in `~/devenv/brain-demo/VERIFICATION.md`: 12 edge shapes, 6 render modes with zero overflow and zero partial escapes at 40/60/80/200, and the flaky test proven pre-existing on unmodified `main` (fails 2 of 3) before being resolved by putting the UI on the branch that already had #351.
