{"id":"COR-2162","uuid":"1a788926-1147-4b77-89fd-873f38e120dc","title":"A component stays "failed" after the cause is gone, and two status surfaces disagree about it","description":"Found live on a developer machine, 2026-10-16, against the installed brain (v0.1.0) for `gh/entirehq/devenv`.

## Observed

`brain_status` reports the `patterns` component as:

```
"name": "patterns", "state": "failed",
"detail": "parse brain manifest: memory_state_corrupt: brain manifest cannot be
           parsed: json: unknown field \"suppressed_warnings\""
```

`brain_patterns_status`, called seconds later, reports:

```
"present": true, "freshness": "current"
```

with `last_run.at = 2026-10-11T22:58:10Z` and every counter zero.

**Two tools, opposite verdicts, same moment.** A user reading one gets "healthy", the other "corrupt". Both ship on the GA MCP surface.

## The cause no longer exists

I scanned **every** `manifest.json` under the brain data directory — **35 files, 0 contain** `suppressed_warnings`. The current `devenv` manifest is `schema_version: 3` with a `warnings` key and no such field.

So the component has been pinned to `failed` since **2026-10-11** — four days — for a condition that is no longer true, and nothing retries it or clears the state.

## What is NOT the bug

The strict/tolerant split is **deliberate and correct**, and should not be "fixed":

* `loadBrainManifest` (readers) tolerates unknown fields.
* `loadBrainManifestForReplace` (writers) refuses them, because "re-encoding from a struct that never saw them erases what another build recorded. Availability is the reader's concern; not destroying state is this one's."

`patterns` is a writer, so refusing was right. `isUnknownFieldError` also works — the prefix `json: unknown field ` matches the raw decoder error, and the tolerant path exists as far back as v0.1.0.

## The three real defects

1. **The message blames corruption for a recoverable, understood condition.** `memory_state_corrupt` reads as data loss. The truth is "another build wrote a field this build does not know, and a writer will not silently erase it." Same class as <issue id="6a801d14-d75c-4d51-aab7-15d6b45e7f0d" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2150/everything-brain-prints-must-be-something-the-reader-can-actually-run">COR-2150</issue> and <issue id="fd72bd11-f77f-4934-b26d-3b99e92f4168" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2146/entire-graph-a-promisor-remote-makes-the-semantic-snapshot-identity">COR-2146</issue>: a correct refusal reported uselessly, with no remedy named.
2. **The failure is sticky.** Once recorded, it survives the cause disappearing. Nothing re-tries, so a transient becomes permanent.
3. **Two surfaces disagree**, and neither defers to the other.

## Done when

The refusal names the unknown field and the remedy instead of saying corrupt; a component failure is re-evaluated rather than latched; and `brain_status` and `brain_patterns_status` cannot report contradictory health for the same component (a test should assert they agree).","projectMilestone":{"id":"bc05f7ea-a603-4d11-bcdc-d9ef4afb9d74","name":"M2 Close the brain blockers"},"priority":{"value":0,"name":"No priority"},"url":"https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2162/a-component-stays-failed-after-the-cause-is-gone-and-two-status","gitBranchName":"suhaan/cor-2162-a-component-stays-failed-after-the-cause-is-gone-and-two","createdAt":"2026-10-16T01:57:04.618Z","updatedAt":"2026-10-16T01:57:04.618Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":[],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Suhaan Thayyil","createdById":"383d093a-5c76-4a6c-9c2b-660b61ca3f3d","project":"P0 · GA the Local Brain","projectId":"91954c69-3fab-4281-84e0-cf4b81d85d75","team":"Core","teamId":"894690b6-2173-4cbe-abd3-6e7ea5ff5bb9"}

The following skills are available for use with the Skill tool:

- audit: Use when asked to "/audit", to audit code, or to make sure changes are bug-free. Runs a review-fix-reverify loop over the code from two lenses (normal code review AND adversarial bugbot-style hunting), fixing every issue, and repeating until two consecutive passes find nothing new with build/lint/tests green.
- entire-cli: Use when working on the `entire` CLI itself (repo entireio/cli — the `cli/` checkout in devenv) — building a new command, fixing a CLI bug, or refreshing the locally installed `entire` binary. Loads the CLI's internal structure, how it talks to entiredb (core + data plane) and entire-api (cells), the checkpoint/agent/plugin/networking internals, the trail/MCP/doctor/telemetry command surface, and the verified build/test/install workflow.
- graph-bench-forensics: Measure whether a code-intelligence tool (entire-graph, cmm, any retrieval MCP) actually saves an agent tokens, by reading every session transcript and decomposing tool calls into token cost. Use when benchmarking a tool arm against a no-tool baseline, when a token-savings claim needs verifying or reproducing, or when a measured saving disagrees with a previous result.
- grilling: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan or design. Use when the user wants to stress-test a plan before building, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.
- makepr: Use when asked to "/makepr" or to create/open a pull request. Produces a clean professional PR with conventional scoped commits, NO Claude/AI session links or footers, and NO references to people or conversations ("Thomas said this", "reply to him", "per the thread"). The commit and PR stand on their own technical merits.
- notepad: Show and update the live campaign notepad — what is running, done, blocked, and next, plus the current work sequence. Use when the user asks "what's the state", "notepad", "where are we", "what's running", "savings", "sequence", or after anything material changes (a cell finishes, a finding is confirmed or retracted, a harness fix lands).
- response: Use when asked to "/response", or to write a reply for Slack/Discord/chat, or whenever the user wants short human-style answers. Writes concise bulleted messages with NO em-dashes and no flowing essay prose, like a real engineer typing in a team channel.
- court: Put an idea on trial. Two adversarial advocates argue it fails and succeeds, twelve independent jurors vote, a judge rules on what is actually weak, and the idea is rewritten and retried until it survives. Use when asked to stress-test, pressure-test, red-team or "put on trial" a plan, pitch, design or decision, or when the user invokes /court.
- trail-findings: Clear agent-review findings off Entire trails so a PR is defensible before human review. Use when asked to run the counter loop, clear findings, unblock the Entire Gates findings sub-gate, or make queued PRs review-ready. Not for opening new PRs.
- codex:rescue: Delegate investigation, an explicit fix request, or follow-up rescue work to the Codex rescue subagent
- codex:setup: Check whether the local Codex CLI is ready and optionally toggle the stop-time review gate
- vercel:bootstrap: Bootstrap a repository with Vercel-linked resources by running preflight checks, provisioning integrations, verifying env keys, and then executing db/dev startup commands safely.

G add go.mod internal/money && G commit -q -m "feat(money): exact amounts in minor units

A float64 cannot hold 0.10, so a thousand dime charges drift away from the
number on the receipt. Amount is int64 minor units with the currency's
exponent carried alongside, so JPY renders without a decimal point and USD
with two."
G add internal/store internal/ledger && G commit -q -m "feat(ledger): append-only double-entry journal

Entries are never updated or deleted. A refund is a new pair, not an edit to
the original, so the balance stays derivable by replay and a dispute is still
answerable months later. Both sides are appended in one call: a crash between
them would leave the journal unbalanced."
G add internal/charge && G commit -q -m "feat(charge): require an idempotency key

The network loses responses, so a client cannot tell a timeout from a success
and will retry. Without a key that retry is a second charge. A replay returns
the original; a replay with a different body is refused rather than honoured,
because the same key meaning two amounts is a client bug."
G add internal/webhook/verify.go && G commit -q -m "feat(webhook): verify provider signatures

Secrets is a set so a rotation overlap does not reject real traffic.
Comparison is hmac.Equal, never ==, because a short-circuiting compare leaks
how much of the prefix matched. A timestamp tolerance stops one captured
signature being valid forever."
G add internal/webhook/handler.go internal/api cmd && G commit -q -m "feat(api): routes, and answer an early capture with 409

The provider can deliver charge.captured before our own write commits. A
handler that treats not-found as fatal drops real captures under load. 409
asks for a retry; 200 would lose the event and 500 would get the endpoint
disabled."
G add -A && G commit -q -m "test: pin the behaviours the design notes claim

Covers replay-does-not-double-bill, duplicate capture not doubling the
ledger, exact dime summation, rotation-window verification and replay
rejection."
G log --oneline | cat

input.command:
D=$(cat "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/acme_build.txt"); cd "$D"
cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# Acme Payments

A small, deliberately realistic payments service — used as a **demo space for
Entire Brain**.

It is here so Brain has something true to index: real packages, real call
relationships, real HTTP routes, and a handful of design decisions whose
*reasons* are not visible in the code. That last part is the point. Anyone can
read `Create` and see that an idempotency key is required. Only the recorded
history says **why** a reused key with a different body is refused instead of
honoured.

## What it does

```
POST /v1/charges              create a charge (Idempotency-Key required)
GET  /v1/charges/{id}         read one charge
GET  /v1/charges/{id}/ledger  the append-only journal for that charge
POST /v1/webhooks/provider    signed provider callbacks
GET  /healthz
```

## Layout

| package | responsibility |
|---|---|
| `internal/money` | exact amounts in minor units |
| `internal/charge` | charge creation, idempotency, capture |
| `internal/ledger` | append-only double-entry journal |
| `internal/webhook` | signature verification + callback handling |
| `internal/store` | persistence seam (in-memory implementation) |
| `internal/api` | HTTP routes |

## Run it

```bash
go test ./...
go run ./cmd/payments        # ADDR=:8080 by default
```

## The decisions worth asking Brain about

Each of these is recorded as a durable fact, so `entire brain recall` can
answer the *why* rather than re-deriving it from the code:

1. **Amounts are int64 minor units, never float.** `0.10` has no exact float
   representation, so a thousand dime charges drift from the receipt.
2. **The idempotency key is required, not optional.** A lost response is
   indistinguishable from a failure, so clients retry — and an unkeyed retry
   is a second charge.
3. **A reused key with a different body is an error, not a new charge.**
4. **The ledger is append-only.** A refund is a new entry pair; nothing is
   ever edited, so the balance is replayable.
5. **Webhook secrets are a set, not a value** — rotation needs an overlap
   window or real traffic gets rejected mid-rollout.
6. **An early capture returns 409, not 200 or 500.** The provider's callback
   can beat our own write; 409 asks for a retry, 200 loses the event, 500 gets
   the endpoint disabled.

Try:

```bash
entire brain recall "why is the idempotency key required" --json
entire brain recall "why 409 and not 500 on an early capture" --json
entire graph query --repo . --query "where are charges captured"
entire graph impact --repo . --symbol Capture
```
EOF
G() { git -c user.email="suhaan@entire.io" -c user.name="Suhaan Thayyil" "$@"; }
G add README.md && G commit -q -m "docs: explain what this demo is for and what to ask Brain"
G push -q origin main 2>&1 | tail -3; echo "pushed: $(G log --oneline -1)"

R 'The Idempotency-Key header is REQUIRED on charge creation, not optional. A payments API runs over a network that loses responses, so a client cannot distinguish a timeout from a success and will retry; an unkeyed retry is a second charge against one intent. R 'A replay with the same Idempotency-Key but a DIFFERENT body returns ErrKeyReusedWithNewBody (HTTP 409), not a new charge. R 'The ledger is append-only double-entry: entries are never updated or deleted, and a refund is a NEW entry pair rather than an edit to the original. R 'Webhook verification holds a SET of secrets, not one value, because rotation needs an overlap window: during a rollout the provider may still sign with the previous secret, and a verifier holding only the newest rejects real traffic for the length of the rotation.' architecture.webhook.decision decision
R 'Webhook signature comparison uses hmac.Equal, never ==. A byte-by-byte string compare returns as soon as it finds a mismatch, so its timing reveals how much of the prefix was correct and a few thousand attempts recover the signature.' constraints.webhook.invariant invariant
R 'GOTCHA: the provider can deliver charge.captured BEFORE our own Create has committed - their network hop is often faster than our write. R 'Capture is idempotent on purpose: a second charge.captured for an already-captured charge returns nil without writing ledger entries again. Providers retry webhooks as normal traffic, so treating a duplicate as an error or re-appending the pair would double the recorded revenue.' architecture.charge.invariant invariant

content.text: `bundle export/import` exists — but bundles **replace** the recipient's brain, and the format can drift between versions. For a demo repo, a readable seed script is safer and it doubles as documentation. Adding both options:

input.command:
D=$(cat "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/acme_build.txt"); cd "$D"; mkdir -p scripts
cat > scripts/seed-brain.sh <<'SCRIPT'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Seed this repo's Entire Brain with the design decisions behind the code.
#
# Durable facts live in YOUR LOCAL brain, not in git. The default fact backend
# (local-gitmeta) is explicitly "fully local, no network", so cloning this repo
# does NOT bring the facts with it. Run this once after cloning and `brain recall`
# will answer the "why" questions the README lists.
#
#   ./scripts/seed-brain.sh
#
# Facts are BRANCH-SCOPED, which is why every call passes --branch main: a fact
# recorded on a feature branch is invisible to someone sitting on main.
#
# Running this twice records the facts twice. It is a seed, not a sync.
set -euo pipefail

BRAIN="${ENTIRE_BRAIN_BIN:-$HOME/.local/share/entire/plugins/bin/entire-brain}"
BRANCH="${BRANCH:-main}"

if [ ! -x "$BRAIN" ]; then
  echo "entire-brain not found at $BRAIN" >&2
  echo "install it:  curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/entireio/entire-brain/main/scripts/get-brain.sh | bash" >&2
  exit 1
fi

remember() { # <path> <kind> <text>
  "$BRAIN" remember "$3" --path "$1" --kind "$2" --branch "$BRANCH" --json >/dev/null
  echo "  recorded: $1"
}

echo "Seeding durable facts on branch '$BRANCH'..."

remember architecture.money.decision decision \
'Amounts are int64 MINOR units (cents), never float64. float64 cannot represent 0.10 exactly, so summing a thousand dime charges drifts from the figure the customer was shown, and a ledger that disagrees with the receipt is not a ledger. money.Currency carries an Exponent so JPY renders with no decimals and USD with two.'

remember architecture.charge.decision decision \
'The Idempotency-Key header is REQUIRED on charge creation, not optional. A payments API runs over a network that loses responses, so a client cannot distinguish a timeout from a success and will retry; an unkeyed retry is a second charge against one intent. Refusing the request with 400 is better than taking the money and arguing later.'

remember architecture.charge.invariant invariant \
'A replay with the same Idempotency-Key but a DIFFERENT body returns ErrKeyReusedWithNewBody (HTTP 409), not a new charge. One key meaning two amounts is a client bug, and quietly honouring the second would charge an amount the first caller never agreed to.'

remember architecture.ledger.invariant invariant \
'The ledger is append-only double-entry: entries are never updated or deleted, and a refund is a NEW entry pair rather than an edit to the original. That keeps the balance derivable by replay, which is what makes a dispute answerable months later. Both sides are appended in a single Append call so a crash cannot leave the journal unbalanced.'

remember architecture.webhook.decision decision \
'Webhook verification holds a SET of secrets, not one value, because rotation needs an overlap window: during a rollout the provider may still sign with the previous secret, and a verifier holding only the newest rejects real traffic for the length of the rotation.'

remember constraints.webhook.invariant invariant \
'Webhook signature comparison uses hmac.Equal, never ==. A byte-by-byte string compare returns as soon as it finds a mismatch, so its timing reveals how much of the prefix was correct and a few thousand attempts recover the signature.'

remember architecture.webhook.gotcha gotcha \
'GOTCHA: the provider can deliver charge.captured BEFORE our own Create has committed - their network hop is often faster than our write. The handler answers store.ErrNotFound with HTTP 409, not 500 and not 200. 409 makes the provider retry with backoff and the charge exists by the next delivery; 200 makes it stop retrying and the capture is lost; 500 gets the endpoint marked unhealthy and disabled.'

remember architecture.charge.invariant invariant \
'Capture is idempotent on purpose: a second charge.captured for an already-captured charge returns nil without writing ledger entries again. Providers retry webhooks as normal traffic, so treating a duplicate as an error or re-appending the pair would double the recorded revenue.'

echo
echo "Done. Try:"
echo "  entire brain recall \"why is the idempotency key required\" --json"
echo "  entire brain recall \"why 409 and not 500 on an early capture\" --json"
SCRIPT
chmod +x scripts/seed-brain.sh
bash -n scripts/seed-brain.sh && echo "syntax OK"
command -v shellcheck >/dev/null && shellcheck scripts/seed-brain.sh && echo "shellcheck clean" || echo "(shellcheck not installed, skipped)"

**Demo space is ready:** https://github.com/entireio/acme-payments

## What's in it

A real Go payments service — not a toy. 7 packages, ~700 lines, `go build` and `go test` green, `vet` clean:

```
POST /v1/charges              Idempotency-Key required
GET  /v1/charges/{id}
GET  /v1/charges/{id}/ledger
POST /v1/webhooks/provider    HMAC-verified
GET  /healthz
```

`money` · `charge` · `ledger` · `webhook` · `store` · `api` — with genuine call relationships and Go HTTP routes, so **Graph** has real edges and routes to show, not a stub.

**8 commits** with messages that explain the reasoning, so session/checkpoint history has substance.

## The part that makes it a *Brain* demo

Eight durable facts recorded — the **why** you can't read off the code:

- int64 minor units, never float — `0.10` has no exact float
- idempotency key **required**, because a lost response is indistinguishable from failure
- reused key + different body → 409, not a second charge
- ledger append-only; a refund is a new pair, so balances replay
- webhook secrets are a **set** — rotation needs an overlap window
- `hmac.Equal`, never `==` — timing leaks the prefix
- **the gotcha:** the provider's capture can beat your own write → 409, because 200 loses the event and 500 disables the endpoint

Verified each is retrievable by a natural question — right fact ranked first every time.

## One thing I had to solve, and you should know about

**Facts don't travel with a clone.** The default backend is `local-gitmeta` — *"fully local, no network"*. Joseph clones the repo and gets **zero facts**.

So I added `scripts/seed-brain.sh` and **proved it works in an isolated brain** (`ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR` + XDG overrides): clean store → run script → recall answers correctly. Joseph runs one command after cloning.

That's also a nice unplanned demo of the P1 gap — hosted sync is what would make this automatic.
